name: Albany County
intro: Albany County sits at the center of the Capital Region, home to the state capital and its suburbs along the Hudson. The Albany County Department for Aging helps residents 60 and older with caregiver support, legal help, NY Connects referrals, adult day programs and in-home check-ins. Its ride partner is ACCESS Transit Services, a CDTA service that books trips for older residents with no other way to reach medical visits, pharmacies, grocery stores and meal sites.

places.note: All galleries and public spaces are wheelchair accessible, with lifts in the main atrium and sculpture gallery, and visitors 62 and older pay $10.

name: Brooklyn (Kings County)
intro: Brooklyn sits across the East River from Manhattan, and older Brooklynites get help through NYC Aging. The agency's older adult centers serve daily meals, and it also offers caregiver help and job help for people who want to keep working. Call Aging Connect at 212-AGING-NYC (212-244-6469) or 311 to ask about Pop-Up Produce and other programs near you.

The Clinton County Office for the Aging helps residents with health and wellness, housing, nutrition, transportation, Medicare questions and NY Connects. For getting around, the office points older riders to Clinton County Public Transit, which runs bus and rural zone service.

The Columbia County Office for the Aging offers home delivered and senior center meals, NY Connects, HIICAP, legal help and a caregiver respite program. For medical visits, the free Children and Adults Rural Transportation Service (CARTS) offers door to door rides, booked through the Healthcare Consortium.

Older residents are served by the Warren/Hamilton Counties Office for the Aging, which has a toll free line for Hamilton County callers at 1-888-553-4994. The office offers scheduled town transportation in Long Lake, Lake Pleasant and Wells, plus volunteer rides to medical appointments.

The agency supports older adult centers, caregiver help, a social adult day care finder and help for older adults facing elder abuse or crime. For any of it, call Aging Connect at 212-AGING-NYC (212-244-6469) or dial 311.
